title: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

relationships.phenotype: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.

checks.claim: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper supports homozygous ABCA2 variants in global developmental delay/intellectual disability (GDD/ID), but it does not use the IDPOGSA name or mention poor growth, seizures or ataxia. It also frames the phenotype as a possible distinct allelic disorder.

paragraphs.text: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is an autosomal recessive neurologic disorder caused by biallelic truncating variants in ABCA2. Reported patients had global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Maddirevula et al., 2019). Patients in a second family had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria (Aslam and Naz, 2019).

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive neurologic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is implied by homozygous variants segregating in autozygous families, but the paper never explicitly calls the ABCA2 disorder autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is caused by biallelic truncating variants in ABCA2.
checks.evidence_quote: fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38]) and (NM_212533.2:c.1027C>T:p.[Gln343*])
checks.explanation: Homozygous truncating variants are biallelic truncating variants.

checks.claim: Patients with ABCA2-related IDPOGSA reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) had global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Patients with ABCA2-related disorder in the family reported by Aslam and Naz (2019) had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) reported 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. Facial photographs of the index patient in 1 family (16DG0071) showed no obvious gross dysmorphism. Maddirevula et al. (2019) noted that this phenotype differed from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis previously reported in association with ABCA2 by Steinberg et al. They suggested that it might represent a distinct allelic disorder.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) reported 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability associated with ABCA2.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Facial photographs of the index patient in family 16DG0071 showed no obvious gross dysmorphism.
checks.evidence_quote: Facial pictures of index (16DG0071) subject with ABCA2 showing apparent lack of gross dysmorphism.
checks.explanation: 16DG0071 is the index subject's ID. The draft's wording 'family 16DG0071' is a minor rewording and does not change the meaning.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) noted that the developmental delay/intellectual disability phenotype differed from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis previously reported in association with ABCA2 by Steinberg et al.
checks.evidence_quote: which is distinct from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) suggested that the ABCA2-related developmental delay/intellectual disability phenotype might represent a distinct allelic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: In class 3, the phenotypes observed are sufficiently different from those previously reported that we argue these may represent distinct allelic disorders
checks.explanation: ABCA2 is listed among the class 3 genes.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with a movement disorder. Their symptoms fit cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Magnetic resonance imaging of the older sib showed no brain abnormalities. Blood low density lipoprotein levels were raised in both affected individuals. The authors noted that the patients' phenotype closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with a movement disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The study was conducted to identify the molecular basis of a movement disorder in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
checks.explanation: The Methods section of the abstract mentions two affected siblings.

checks.claim: The symptoms of the 2 Pakistani sibs studied by Aslam and Naz (2019) fit cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Magnetic resonance imaging of the older of the 2 Pakistani sibs showed no brain abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: We performed clinical assessments and magnetic resonance imaging of the older of two siblings affected with a movement disorder.
checks.explanation: The Results add: 'Magnetic resonance imaging did not reveal brain abnormalities.'

checks.claim: Blood low density lipoprotein levels were raised in both affected Pakistani sibs studied by Aslam and Naz (2019).
checks.evidence_quote: The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) noted that the phenotype of the Pakistani sibs closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotype observed in our patients shows high concordance with that observed in Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) found raised blood low density lipoprotein levels in 2 sibs with ABCA2-related ataxia and dysarthria.

checks.evidence_quote: The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the families reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. In these families, homozygous ABCA2 variants fully segregated with the disorder. Aslam and Naz (2019) also considered the disorder in their consanguineous family to be recessively inherited.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of IDPOGSA in the families reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Autosomal recessive transmission is inferred from homozygous segregation, but the paper does not explicitly describe it.

checks.claim: In the families reported by Maddirevula et al. (2019), homozygous ABCA2 variants fully segregated with the disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) considered the ABCA2-related disorder in their consanguineous family to be recessively inherited.
checks.evidence_quote: Although recessively inherited ABCA2 variants have been reported in two patients who had intellectual disability with global developmental delays, our study demonstrates the role of an ABCA2 variant
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is implied by the consanguinity and the comparison, but the abstract does not explicitly say the authors considered their own family's disorder recessive.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) searched the autozygome and exome data of patients with suspected Mendelian phenotypes. In 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability, they identified 2 different homozygous truncating mutations in the ABCA2 gene: a 1-bp duplication (c.740dupT), predicted to cause a frameshift (Gly248ArgfsTer38), and a c.1027C-T transition causing a gln343-to-ter (Q343X) substitution. Both mutations fully segregated with the disorder in their respective families.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) searched the autozygome and exome data of patients with suspected Mendelian phenotypes.
checks.evidence_quote: Autozygome and exome analysis of patients with suspected Mendelian phenotypes.
checks.explanation: The paper's methods state this directly.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified 2 different homozygous truncating ABCA2 mutations in 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Two different truncating variants were found in two families.

checks.claim: One ABCA2 mutation identified by Maddirevula et al. (2019) was a 1-bp duplication (c.740dupT) predicted to cause a frameshift (Gly248ArgfsTer38).
checks.evidence_quote: ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])
checks.explanation: The variant notation matches, and c.740dupT is a 1-bp duplication.

checks.claim: One ABCA2 mutation identified by Maddirevula et al. (2019) was a c.1027C-T transition causing a gln343-to-ter (Q343X) substitution.
checks.explanation: Equivalent notation.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.740dupT and Q343X mutations each fully segregated with the disorder in their respective families.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Both variants segregated with the disorder.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied 2 affected sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria. Using whole-exome sequencing, they identified a 1-bp deletion in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG), predicted to cause a frameshift (Val1665TyrfsTer36). Sanger sequencing showed that the variant segregated with the disorder. The variant was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls.

checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.

checks.explanation: c.4993delG is a 1-bp deletion.

checks.explanation: The abstract gives the same protein change.

checks.explanation: The Results state that the variant segregated with the disorder.
